classification.difficultyReason: Parts a and b are direct applications of inverse tangent. The opposite and adjacent sides are read off a labelled right triangle, and the two parts differ only in which angle is used. Part c is guided: adding the two answers shows they make 90°. Part d is the hardest essential demand. The student must see that 5/12 and 12/5 are the two acute angles of one right triangle, and then use the complement from part c instead of calculating. This is a single reframing, and part c signposts it. It is more demanding than p35-q8, which needs only one trig choice in a half-triangle. It is less demanding than p36-q10, which needs two separate angle calculations and a comparison with a judgement about 'half'.

content.prompt: Refer to the diagram to complete the following.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Add your answers to parts a and b. What do you notice?

answer.worked:
$$53.1^{\circ}+36.9^{\circ}=90.0^{\circ}$$
The two acute angles of a right-angled triangle add to $90^{\circ}$, since the angles of a triangle add to $180^{\circ}$ and one angle is $90^{\circ}$. So $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)=90^{\circ}$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Given that $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5}{12}\right)\approx22.6^{\circ}$, write down $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{12}{5}\right)$ without using a calculator. Answer to 1 d.p.

answer.worked:
The ratios $\frac{5}{12}$ and $\frac{12}{5}$ give the two acute angles of the same right-angled triangle.
$$\begin{align*}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{12}{5}\right)&=90^{\circ}-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{12}\right)\\&\approx90^{\circ}-22.6^{\circ}\\&=67.4^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
